title: The surfactant ring of the ringed active-nematic rods survives a 1.5x finer grid (interface/interior 2.24 vs 2.47-2.50 at dx=1; chi_s=0: 0.80); labkit's centroid radial test understates rings on long rods
summary: Re-ran my ringed-rod world (20261025T1141-c11-active-nematic-ringed) on a 1.5x finer grid at the same physical size (dx 2/3, 192^2), seed 0, with and without adsorption (chi_s=0). The colony forms from one nucleus as in 20261025T1036-c11-active-nematic-res15 (6 persistent splits, gen 3, 11 tracks >= 1 BL), and the crops show a bright surfactant ring along every rod's phi=0 contour (ring_res15.png). Measured by phi band over frames >= 100 (bandring.py: interface |phi|<0.5, interior phi>0.6, near outside phi<-0.8 within 4 px): interface/interior 2.24 and interface/outside 5.76 at 1.5x, against 2.47-2.50 and 4.94-5.09 on seeds 0-2 at dx=1; chi_s=0 gives 0.80 and 1.35-1.36 at both grids (bandring.txt). labkit's radial test (rho = r/R_eq around the centroid) gives only rim/core 1.04 and 11/35 membrane-like at 1.5x, because the finer grid resolves longer, bent rods whose centroid falls near their own wall; the band measure does not depend on the body's shape.

finding.operator: self-made surfactant drifting up the interface indicator 1 - phi^2 on active-nematic rods
finding.control: 1.5x grid refinement at fixed physical size, with the chi_s=0 ablation at both grids
finding.result: interface/interior s: 2.47-2.50 (dx=1, 3 seeds), 2.24 (1.5x); chi_s=0 0.80; interface/outside 4.9-5.8 vs 1.35

limits: One seed at the finer grid. The ring is passive (it does not act back), as stated in the claim. bandring.py pools all bodies and frames; it does not test each body separately.
